title: A `@mandate` that fails admission fails every mandate-gated decision closed, and admission refuses a stated `authority.moves []`
summary: Breaking: 2.0.0 admitted a `@mandate` stating `authority.moves []`, and a mandate that failed admission was dropped from the admitted graph, so it silently stopped restricting: a mandate stating `moves [Bogus]` and `excluded-words [task]` let `ia preview task` run, where the same mandate with valid moves refused it (operator ruling 2026-10-12: fail closed for any `@mandate` that fails admission, reject `moves []` in the schema, the refusal names the record, `ia position` and hand edits still work). @inventarch/compliance: schema field validation, which db admission (validateGraphSchema) and the bootstrap validateSchema both run, refuses a stated empty authority.moves on a record whose word is `mandate`, when its schema declares that key as agent-system's does, with IA-COMP-FIELD-VALUE, an error at that field, each such occurrence on its own, whose message says 'authority.moves' must name at least one kernel move when stated; an absent authority.moves stays valid and restricts no move, and every other empty list stays valid (compliance C05 states this one exception). A workspace 2.0.0 admitted with `moves []` therefore has an admission error now: the machine routes keep their shapes, but over such a workspace the report route lists the finding and the read routes no longer return that mandate. @inventarch/db: every read handle and editor snapshot exposes unadmitted, with the UnadmittedRecord and UnadmittedFinding types: each record occurrence of the root view's sources that it does not admit, {identity?, word?, name?, band, path, line, endLine, finding}, for each occurrence refused names, both occurrences of an identity tie, and each record of a file refused whole by a language error or a duplicate requirement id; band is the band of the source's placement (100 authored, 90 for an adopted or installed base), and finding {code, path, line, message} the record's own admission finding from the diagnostics db already holds. A file refused whole is read from db's own parse (with the identity its compile gives, or spec 3.1's for a header the compile refused) and from its captured text, split at CRLF, CR or LF: a line opening with `@<word>` after any whitespace or Unicode format characters, which the parse did not read as a header, is listed with the name after it, wherever it stands, inside a parsed record too; on a line no parsed record spans every `@<word>` token is listed under its word; and a line that names no header is listed with no word, a record db cannot identify, when it holds one of the file's errors and no parsed record spans it (an error at a blank or `#` comment line being taken at the first line from there that is neither, so an empty or comment-only file lists nothing), when it opens with an at sign (`@`, U+FF20 or U+FE6B) after any whitespace or format characters, wherever it stands, or, in a file refused at its pragma, when it stands at column 0 and is neither blank nor a comment: a header spelled `@ mandate x`, with a full-width at sign or with a joiner after the at sign, UTF-16LE text without a byte-order mark, a stray top-level line; an error inside a parsed record's lines on a line no at sign opens stays that record's; refused, the report, the snapshot and the cache are unchanged, and nothing more is read from disk. @inventarch/runtime: the package root and ./internal/mandate-modes export refusedMandates(handle) with the RefusedMandate type, every authored (band 100) `@mandate` that failed admission, by path then line, each {identity?, path, line, code, message, unidentified?} with its own admission finding, an occurrence db lists with no word counting as a possible mandate, marked unidentified, so an authored file refused whole whose records db cannot all identify fails closed, as far as db's readings reach; a mandate refused in an installed base (band 90) never counts. They also export refusedDependencies(handle), with the RefusedDependency type {dependent, field, reference, identity?, path, line, code, message}: each admitted authored `@mandate` whose authority.participant names a refused `@agent` or whose authority.scope names a refused `@workspace`, and each `@workspace` whose composition.steward names a refused `@agent`, each reference matched as authored by word and name against db's band-100 unadmitted entries, a line of a file refused whole opening `@agent <name>` or `@workspace <name>` among them; without this, a refused participant or steward `@agent` switched the default actor to another participant with looser mandates, and a refused `@workspace` left a scope-only mandate governing nowhere. A refused `@agent` or `@workspace` nothing names, a reference no authored record answers, and a record refused in an installed base keep today's reading. While either returns anything, requireMandatesAdmitted(handle, within), which governingMandates, seatedWorkspace and defaultActor call first, throws IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID marked admission 'refused' (isAdmissionRefusal(error) reads the mark), deciding workspace-wide whatever the scope token, since a refused record's scope, covers and participant cannot be trusted; through a whole-workspace token the error names the first refused mandate db identifies, else the first it cannot, as an unidentified record at path:line, possibly a `@mandate`, counting the rest by kind, else the first dependency and the record that depends on it, with the refused record's identity when known, path:line, admission code and message, and locates it as where; through a narrowed token it names no path, record or finding and carries no where. RuntimeError gains optional fourth and fifth constructor arguments, a frozen where {path, line, identity?} (the RuntimeWhere type), which that refusal and every mandateAuthorityOf refusal carry, and admission; profileRefusal and mandateRefusal keep their own empty-move-list refusal. admissionReport(root?) spells the admission report command, `ia report --root <root>` with forward slashes on win32 only when every character of the root is a letter, a digit or one of `._-/:`, else `ia report` to run from the workspace root, never a root in double quotes. evaluateMandateGuard's request takes an optional root and its decision an optional where; it branches on isAdmissionRefusal: while a record a mandate resolution reads fails admission every edit the hook selects is IA-HOOK-MANDATE-UNAVAILABLE, whoever acts, naming the refused record's path:line, its finding and admissionReport(root) rather than `ia validate`, and an admitted mandate whose authority cannot be read still names its governance position. @inventarch/cli: while an authored `@mandate` fails admission, or a record an admitted mandate or workspace depends on does, `ia read`, `ia next`, `ia validate`, `ia preview`, `ia author`, `ia capture` (and `ia capture --preview`), `ia compile`, `ia project` and a workspace `ia host <host> --apply` refuse with IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID at exit 1, a where of {path, line, identity} at the first such record (identity null when unknown) and a message naming the record and its admission finding and saying a hand edit corrects it, since `ia preview` and `ia author` cannot target a record admission refused; it classifies the refusal by the runtime's mark, so a refused authored mandate sharing its identity with an admitted one of another band is no exception. The next command is the version 1 machine route `ia report`, which no mandate gates and which prints the admission report with the finding (exit 1 for a failing report, nothing on stderr): with the invocation's --root as every next command repeats it, else with the root spelled relative to the working directory (`.` or `..` segments only) when that spelling, resolved from the working directory as the route resolves --root, reaches the same real root (relative to the working directory as given first, which on win32 keeps a junction's spelling, then to its real path, so a junction or directory symlink in the path still names a root that runs), else `ia report` run from the workspace root with no path printed. An admitted mandate whose authority the runtime cannot read, such as one with a child under authority.moves, still refuses naming its governance position, now with where {path, line, identity}. `ia position`, `ia host <host> --remove --apply` (which still restores editing), `--user`, the Door and MCP reads, the install refresh, `ia-distribution`, `ia inspect` and `ia init` are unchanged and keep running. @inventarch/steward-hook: the `--hook` guard passes the registration's root to evaluateMandateGuard, so a refusal at a refused record names the admission report as admissionReport spells it; the main session's refusal still also names `ia host claude --root <root> --remove --apply --yes`; an edit the hook does not select is still not decided and managed-state protection is unchanged; a registration whose hook is not admitted, or not a declaration it can decide, is IA-HOOK-MANDATE-UNAVAILABLE naming the refused record while one is refused (the hook may share its file); when the records cannot be read, the refusal names `ia validate --root <root>` if the database cannot open at all, and once it opened, the admission report while a refused mandate or dependency is among what admission refused, else `ia validate --root <root>`; a failure while the edit is decided names the admission report. @inventarch/workspace-runtime: unchanged source, but agent-profile generation's fallback for a profile that names no mandate reads governingMandates, so while a record a mandate resolution reads fails admission the rendered agent says the fallback is unavailable and names that record. Limits: the fail-closed is workspace-wide, so one broken record blocks every gated command and selected edit for every actor until its source is corrected by hand, and no in-tool repair exists; in a file refused whole, a line that declares a record with its at sign behind another character on its line (a NUL, a letter, other text) is not seen when it stands inside the lines of a record the parse reads, or indented in a file refused at its pragma, since no reading names it and an error there is that record's (db D15 states the readings exactly), while any line outside such a record that only mentions `@mandate`, any line an at sign opens that names no header, any error line outside a parsed record that names no header, and any top-level line of a file refused at its pragma that is neither blank nor a comment, is read as a possible mandate, failing closed; a mandate in a file db never reads (an extension other than lowercase `.ia`, or a path under node_modules, dist or .git) restricts nothing and is reported nowhere, as in 2.0.0; a --root the invocation gave is repeated as given, as every next command repeats it; position, body(K), the packet renderer and the Door operations render no mandate for a refused record and never refuse; the nine machine routes, MACHINE_PROTOCOL versions 1 and 2 and every `ia scope` form keep their shapes.
